title: Switch off the named circuit breaker in a distribution board
instruction: Switch off the breaker that feeds SOCKETS - KITCHEN (find it on the labels above the breakers or the circuit directory) so that its window reads O-OFF. Leave the other circuits on.
context: Isolating a circuit starts with switching off the right breaker in a row of identical ones, found by matching the circuit's name to the board's labels. Switching off the wrong way leaves the intended circuit live and cuts power to another, and a push that stops short of the breaker's snap point lets it spring back on.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top the bases stand on. Board (fixed to the table, centred on the midline): a light-grey 2 mm steel back pan, 28 cm wide and 27.6 cm tall, stands upright on the table with its front face 39.2 cm in front of the bases. A steel EN 60715 TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail, 26 cm long, is fixed across it, its centre line 15.6 cm above the table. Breakers: six Schneider Acti9 iC60N 1P miniature circuit breakers (18 mm wide, 85 mm tall, white plastic) clip side by side on the rail, the row centred on the midline, their front faces 32 cm in front of the bases. From left to right they are ways 1 to 6, centred 4.5, 2.7 and 0.9 cm left and 0.9, 2.7 and 4.5 cm right of the midline: 1 LIGHTING - WORKSHOP, C10 (A9F74110); 2 HEATERS - OFFICE, C16 (A9F74116); 3 BATTERY CHARGER, C20 (A9F74120); 4 SOCKETS - KITCHEN, C16 (A9F74116); 5 HVAC - AHU-1, C20 (A9F74120); 6 SPARE, C10 (A9F74110). Each handle is a white rocker with a black grip bar (13 mm wide, 5 mm thick) 16 mm from its pivot; the pivots are 14.85 cm above the table. A handle turns 30 degrees either side of centre: up is ON, down is OFF. Its window shows I-ON, or a green O-OFF band, depending on its position. All six start ON. Cover: a light-grey 1.5 mm steel dead-front cover, 26 cm wide and 17 cm tall, is fixed 33.8 cm in front of the bases, centred on the midline and on the rail's height (7.1 to 24.1 cm above the table). Only the breakers' 45 mm-tall fronts pass through its 10.8 cm-wide cut-out (13.35 to 17.85 cm above the table), standing 1.8 cm proud of it. Label strip: on the cover directly above each breaker, a printed paper label (17 mm wide, 18 mm tall; its bottom edge 3 mm above the cut-out, centre 19.1 cm above the table) shows the way number in large print, the circuit name and the rating, on a background coloured by circuit type: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 orange, 4 blue, 5 green, 6 white. Circuit directory: a printed card (5.6 cm wide, 6.2 cm tall) on the cover to the right of the breakers, centre 9.2 cm right of the midline and 15.6 cm above the table (its right edge 1 cm inside the cover's edge), lists the six ways with the same colour swatches, names and ratings. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if any other breaker's handle passes the middle of its travel at any time (it then snaps to OFF). Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the way-4 (SOCKETS - KITCHEN) handle turns 5 degrees or more toward OFF (about 1.5 mm at its bar) at some point; 0.5 if it passes the middle of its travel at some point; 0.75 if it sits at its OFF stop (within 5 degrees) with its window reading O-OFF and the other five handles ON (within 5 degrees of their ON stops) at the end of the run, or when the after-release check starts, but the check fails or is never reached; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. After-release check, done once every fingertip has been at least 4 cm from the way-4 handle's pivot for 1 s with that handle at its OFF stop: push the way-4 grip bar upward (toward ON) with a spring scale at 3.7 N, 17 mm from the pivot (0.063 N m, three quarters of the torque that holds the handle at its stop), for 1.5 s. Pass if the handle stays within 5 degrees of its OFF stop, the window still reads O-OFF, and the other five handles are still ON. Handle angles are read from a side photo with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Push the way-4 handle (and any other handle that was switched) back up until it snaps ON, and check that all six windows read I-ON. About 15 seconds.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Snap action is geometry: a spring plunger on a cam ball holds the handle at either stop (0.084 N·m, inferred from a published study) and snaps it over centre. Throw and pivot read from Schneider's drawing. Simplified: window marking on the handle (no contacts), box colliders, generic print, one rail; labels unreadable overhead but colour-coded; check torque in sim after recording. Details in README.
